thread:
ana: sharing two prototypes for structured-output tool call UX in the playground. Prototype A shows full function signature inline on the result card; Prototype B collapses signature into an expand chevron and shows primary action only. Which reduces clutter without hiding important info?

drew: For scanning, B wins. most devs just want the top-level output + obvious invoke. we can surface the signature in a keyboard-only reveal.

liam: signature is critical when users chain tools. Could we expose a small badge showing arg count and types, e.g., (3 args) ?

aria: accessibility checks: collapsed content must be reachable by screen reader users and the expand control needs aria-expanded + aria-controls. also ensure the badge has descriptive text like "3 arguments: text, url, boolean".

ana: tiny copy nit: label the invoke button "Invoke with args" when args present, otherwise just "Invoke". keeps clarity.

ux-bot: poll started — vote: show-signature-inline, collapse-with-badge, collapse-hide-signature. react to vote.

drew: :thumbsup: collapse-with-badge

liam: :white_check_mark: show-signature-inline

aria: :eyes: collapse-with-badge (a11y-friendly)

ana: plan: we'll prototype collapse-with-badge + keyboard-only expansion. running moderated usability with 6 engineers to validate discoverability and a11y path. will follow up with recordings and recommended ARIA roles.

drew: can we also test how this looks in run history where many entries list invocations? spacing/line-height will be important.

ana: yes — adding run-history density variant to test matrix. thanks all!
